# Native core app kit 1.5.0

Major 1 now defaults to 1.7.0 (read `app-kit-core-1.7.0`). 1.5.0, 1.4.0, 1.3.0, 1.2.0, 1.1.2, 1.1.1, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 are
retained for host rollback. 1.5.0 is compatible with 1.4.0 and adds device checkpoints to safe
writes, so an app can keep an unresolved write across a reload under its original key (below).
It keeps 1.3.0's Paseo agent sessions (Native Desktop only), 1.2.0's safe writes (`useWrite`,
`WriteStatus`, `createWriteHelper`), 1.1.2's Markdown fixes and 1.1.1's quiet read recovery in
`useQueryFeed` and `FeedNotice`.
The host installs frozen `window.native.kit` synchronously before the
first author script. No imports, npm, JSX compiler or build are required.
An unavailable requested major refuses `kit_major_unavailable`.

## Prepare an install from Native MCP alone

Create the complete HTML as a `Document/artifact` with runtime `native.html.v1`.
Use its write receipt's `body_digest` (or body-carrying `source_event_id`) to call
`artifacts_read.manage_alpha_tabs.prepare_install` through `call_executor`:

```json
{"executor":"artifacts_read","operation":"manage_alpha_tabs.prepare_install","arguments":{"artifact_id":"<source id>","expected_body_digest":"<body_digest>","package":"agent.my-app","version":"1.0.0","declaration":{"needs":[],"effects":[]},"reason":"Install my authored app"}}
```

Include your actual consent declaration, including each SQL snapshot need.
When `ready` is true, pass the returned `next_call` to `call_executor`, adding
your `run_key`. It contains the server-computed digests, source revision and
install/update event precondition; no shell, hash computation or build is needed.
When false, read the bounded findings, fix the source/declaration and prepare again.
Malformed package/version/reason/request/guard arguments and authority failures
are normal API errors, rather than `ready:false` findings. Preparation caps the
echoed declaration at 65,536 serialized JSON bytes; `require_declaration` has
entry limits but no total byte cap. An optional `request` is validated and passed
through, including a reinstall over a removed tab; updates must preserve it.
Kit availability is advisory against the packaged default; delivery checks its
own selection. Preparation grants nothing, installs nothing and locks nothing.
The returned revision pins historical bytes; later source edits do not silently
replace them. Re-prepare after edits. Current update CAS and consent rules still
apply. `ready:true` means prepared, not usable. Read `adoption`: when it is
`requires_person_preview_adopt`, tell the signed-in person to Preview/Adopt after
install/update; MCP cannot mint that authority. `carried` means the update can
carry proven adoption for an unchanged canonical declaration. An unadopted
predecessor still requires Preview/Adopt even when the declaration is unchanged.

Alpha tabs pin a package/version/digest, a viewable live `Document/artifact`, its
source revision and consented needs/effects. Updates check exact bytes/digest and
event CAS, preserving status/request. Keyed retries return the original receipt
and current install without reapplying. Disable/restore/remove use event CAS;
disabled or removed tabs stop reads/actions. Target resolution fails closed;
inspect `target_resolves`. List before reorder: reorder replaces the strip order,
appends omitted installs, and refuses unknown/removed/duplicate entries. Without
a saved order, the strip uses agents/folders/tasks/graph/installs.

Preview checks exact source/digest and returns sample HTML with an expiring
account/pin/session receipt; it writes nothing. Preview/adopt/adopt_authored
require a hosted cookie and trusted Origin, never Bearer credentials. Adopt
checks the receipt, pin, event and attestation. Launch checks adoption, event,
View and source; its one-use URL delivers sample input only, without live rows.
`live_read` returns only the caller's authorized consented inputs:
`attention.query.v1` at `input.records`, up to eight `sql.snapshot.v1` SELECT/WITH
needs with 200 rows each at `input.sql[key]`. `params[0]` binds `?1`; omitted
optional parameters bind NULL. Use `live_read.need` to request a consented `records.search.v1` with
`params:{query,limit}` (`limit` at most 30), `records.resolve_reference.v1` with
`params:{reference}`, or a SQL need by key with its declared parameter schema.
Omit `need` for the snapshot. Subscriptions are connection-bound; use the stream-frame token;
subscriptions and `if_revision` apply only to snapshot reads. An `if_revision`
equal to `revision_digest` returns `unchanged:true` with pins/revision and no rows.
Use `if_revision` to resynchronize. Revision information includes `id` and
`time_dependent`; `now_ms()` uses `as_of_ms`. `subscribe_refused` includes the
read. `live_unsubscribe` is idempotent and connection-scoped.
`admit_reveal_target` checks consented `surface.reveal.v1` and one visible
canonical target/pin; delivery is push-only, never via `live_read`.
Supply the full record id or a reserved id such as `native:root`; prefixes refuse.

## A source-only feed app

This complete source-only app displays a declared `records.recent` param-less
`sql.snapshot.v1` feed. Declare that need in the install declaration; the kit
policy below adds no data permission. Use this exact declaration:

```json
{
  "needs": [
    {
      "need": "sql.snapshot.v1",
      "key": "records.recent",
      "label": "Up to 200 visible records, newest first",
      "sql": "SELECT id, substr(name, 1, 160) AS name, type, kind, updated_at FROM records WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM facet_values fv WHERE fv.record_id = records.id AND fv.key = 'archived') ORDER BY updated_at_ms DESC, id ASC LIMIT 200"
    }
  ],
  "effects": []
}
```

The SQL selects `id` and `name`, the columns the example renders. Apps own
CSS; the components use simple `kit-*` classes and add no reset.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Recent notes</title>
<script type="application/json" id="native-app-kit">{"schema":"native.app-kit.v1","major":1}</script>
<style>body{font:16px system-ui;margin:2rem}.kit-record-link{cursor:pointer}</style>
</head><body><main id="app">Opening Native…</main>
<script type="module">
const kit = window.native?.kit;
const root = document.getElementById('app');
if (!kit?.preact) root.textContent = 'Open in a Native host with core kit 1.2.0.';
else {
  const { html, render, useFeed, Loading, Empty, ErrorState, RecordLink } = kit.preact;
  function App() {
    const feed = useFeed('records.recent');
    if (feed.status === 'loading') return html`<${Loading} what="notes" />`;
    const result = feed.status === 'ready' ? feed.result : feed.last;
    return html`<section><h1>Recent notes</h1>
      ${feed.status === 'error' && html`<${ErrorState} error=${feed.error} />`}
      ${feed.status === 'error' && result && html`<p>Last good rows; may be out of date.</p>`}
      ${result && html`<p>${kit.countLabel(result)} notes</p>`}
      ${result?.rows.length ? html`<ul>${result.rows.map(row => html`<li key=${row.id}>
        <${RecordLink} id=${row.id}>${row.name || row.id}<//></li>`)}</ul>`
        : html`<${Empty}>No notes delivered.<//>`}
    </section>`;
  }
  try { await kit.ready; render(html`<${App} />`, root); }
  catch (error) { root.textContent = 'Native could not initialize this app.'; }
  addEventListener('pagehide', () => render(null, root), { once: true });
}
</script></body></html>
```

`kit.preact` supplies one Preact instance: `h`, `render`, `Fragment`,
`createContext`, standard hooks, and `html = htm.bind(h)`. Use its hooks for its
components. `useFeed(key)` uses core snapshots; `useQueryFeed(query)` waits for
ready and uses the optional negotiated app-v2 `window.native.subscribe`.
Equivalent JSON query values keep the subscription; changed queries and
unmounts unsubscribe and suppress late deliveries. Errors retain last-good
rows and delivery time. Inside a v2 component, pass `feed.retry`
to the retry button:

```js
const feed = kit.preact.useQueryFeed({ sql: 'SELECT id, name FROM records LIMIT 20' });
if (feed.status === 'error')
  return html`<${ErrorState} error=${feed.error} onRetry=${feed.retry} />`;
```

`retry()` resubscribes to the same query; a terminal error closes the old
subscription. Hooks mounted after kit disposal return a `closed` error.
Query answers have `truncated`, not a total count.

### Quiet read recovery (1.1.1, unchanged)

`useQueryFeed` keeps the last good rows on screen through errors and retries,
including while a manual `retry()` reloads: the `loading` state carries `last`
and `deliveredAt` for the same query, and a changed query starts clean (except
after a definite answer, below). It also
recovers quietly, so a brief blip never reaches the person:

- Only transient errors keep the saved rows: `offline`, `busy`, `timeout`,
  `unavailable`, `query_timeout`, `network_lost`, `engine_error`,
  `subscription_limit`, `database_pool_timeout`, `http_408/429/5xx` and the hub's
  `authority_changed:<n>` recheck. A *terminal* transient error resubscribes
  after 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds, then stops; a resubscription that stays silent for
  10 seconds counts as failed. A non-terminal one is left to the host's own retry
  and fails after 15 seconds without recovery.
- **Every other error is a definite answer** (`access_denied`, `forbidden`,
  `unauthorized`, `undeclared`, 401/403, `query_refused`, `invalid_sql`,
  `refused`, `port_closed`, any unknown code, terminal or not). It is never
  retried, shows "Couldn’t refresh" with Try again at once, and the kit **drops
  the saved rows** (`last`, `deliveredAt`): the transport cannot tell which
  refusals still leave the old data authorised (an invalidated install arrives as
  a plain `query_refused`). Try again starts clean; only a new answer brings rows
  back.
- `feed.notice` is `'none'` for the first 4 seconds of trouble, `'reconnecting'`
  after that, and `'failed'` once retries are used up or cannot help. A host that
  keeps reporting non-terminal errors reaches `'failed'` after 15 seconds.
- `feed.truncated` is true when the rows shown (current or last good) are only
  part of the answer.
- While recovery is in progress an error carries `error.retrying`
  (`'quiet'` or `'reconnecting'`). `ErrorState` renders nothing for `quiet`,
  "Reconnecting…" for `reconnecting`, and the full error with Try again
  otherwise, so `ErrorState error=${feed.error}` is already quiet. `status`
  stays `'error'` for compatibility; read `notice` and `error.retrying`.

`FeedNotice` renders the notice for you: "Reconnecting…", then "Couldn’t refresh"
with a working Try again, plus "Showing part of the results." when truncated. It
shows nothing when there is nothing to say. Render rows from
`feed.status === 'ready' ? feed.result : feed.last` and add the notice beside them:

```js
const feed = kit.preact.useQueryFeed({ sql: 'SELECT id, name FROM records LIMIT 20' });
const result = feed.status === 'ready' ? feed.result : feed.last;
return html`<section><${FeedNotice} feed=${feed} />${result && renderRows(result.rows)}</section>`;
```

Defaults can be tuned per call: `useQueryFeed(query, { retryDelaysMs: [1000, 2000], noticeDelayMs: 4000 })`.

A ready result is `{ rows, columns, truncated, cached? }`. Rows of a `{ sql }`
query, like snapshot rows, are objects keyed by column name: read `row.id`, not
`row[0]`. `columns` names them in select order. Rows of a structured `{ steps }`
query are arrays aligned with `columns` (`id`, `type`, `kind`, `name`,
`summary`, `home_id`, `lifecycle`, `maturity`, `updated_at`,
`last_activity_at`). To accept either shape, use
`Array.isArray(row) ? Object.fromEntries(columns.map((c, i) => [c, row[i]])) : row`.
A host without subscriptions returns `status: 'unsupported'` with an explicit
message. Core major 1 never grants app-v2 authority to an app-v1 install.

For an app-v2 install, negotiated `query`, `subscribe` and `call` may also be
used directly after `kit.ready`. Check each optional method. A write is saved
only when `call(operation, args).confirmed` resolves; dispatch is not a receipt.
Initial Preview/Adopt still requires the person's browser gesture.

### Safe writes (1.2.0)

Do not hand-roll "key, retry, did it send?" logic. `useWrite` does it, and
`WriteStatus` tells the person the truth:

```js
const { useWrite, WriteStatus, html } = kit.preact;
function NewNote({ folder }) {
  const writes = useWrite({ operation: 'create_record', scope: folder });
  const create = title => writes.submit({ type: 'Document', kind: 'note', name: title,
    home_id: folder, reason: 'Create note from my app' });
  return html`<button onClick=${() => create('Meeting')}>Create note</button>
    ${writes.entries.map(entry => html`<${WriteStatus} key=${entry.id} entry=${entry}
      onRetry=${() => writes.retry(entry.id)} onDiscard=${() => writes.discard(entry.id)} />`)}`;
}
```

- **Freeze and key first.** `submit(request)` copies and freezes the request (plain
  data only) and mints its `idempotency_key` before anything is sent, then calls
  the operation in the same task, so a click is still a click. Later edits to your
  form never change a write already submitted. For `operation`, the kit adds
  `idempotency_key` to the arguments; do not set it yourself. To send some other
  way, pass `dispatch(request, { key, attempt })` and use `key`.
- **Busy retry.** A `busy` or `too_many_in_flight` refusal is retried twice (after
  300 ms and 600 ms) with the same frozen request and key, then reported as not
  sent. Tune with `busyDelaysMs`.
- **Three kinds of ending.** *Definitely not sent*: a `refused` status, or code
  `tool_not_dispatched`, `effect_not_dispatched` or `not_sent_timeout`. *Applied*:
  only when the host affirms the whole write committed: `applied: true` (sent by
  the host with `REPLAY_BOUND_EXCEEDED` when a single write's receipt could not be
  rebuilt). *Possibly applied*: everything else that is not a confirmation: a
  timeout, a lost connection, an unknown code, and also `REPLAY_BOUND_EXCEEDED`
  without `applied: true` or with `applied: "partial"` (a `create_many` with
  unfinished items). A possibly-applied write stays "May not have sent" under its
  original key until a retry confirms it; it cannot be discarded or evicted.
- **Retry identity.** `retry(id)` re-sends the same frozen request. While the
  last attempt may have applied it reuses the key, so Native applies it once; only
  after a definite "not sent" does it mint a new key. A refusal that arrives after
  an uncertain attempt never clears it: the entry stays "May not have sent" with
  its original request and key.
- **Statuses.** Each entry has `status`: `pending`, `sent`, `uncertain` or
  `failed`, and a plain `label` to show: "Sending…", "Sent", "May not have sent"
  (Retry, no alarm) and "Not sent" (Retry or Discard; the person's frozen payload is
  kept until they choose). `canRetry` and `canDiscard` say which buttons make sense;
  an uncertain write cannot be discarded because its key is the only protection
  against a duplicate. `entry.error` carries the host's `code`/`message` if you want
  to word a reason; never show raw codes. Apps should render `label` and switch on
  `status`, not on `custody`.
- **Custody.** Without a checkpoint, entries live only in this page. With a
  device checkpoint, acknowledged entries report `custody: "device"` and
  "Saved on this device"; refusals or a five-second storage timeout still send
  with memory custody and a not-saved notice. Status continues to describe the
  send outcome. Do not exhaustively switch on `custody`.
- **Account boundary.** Pending, uncertain and refused entries are dropped when the
  workspace or account moves: when any mounted `useQueryFeed` hears the hub's
  `scope_changed`, or when the `scope` option's value changes (applied in the commit
  that shows the new scope, never while rendering). Each write is bound to the scope,
  and to the operation or `dispatch`, of the render whose handler submitted it; a later
  render never retargets it. A write submitted by a child's mount effect, before its
  parent's scope has committed, is kept and shown as "Sending…" and goes out when that
  scope commits; if a different scope commits instead, or the component unmounts, it
  is reported "Not sent" and dropped, never sent to the wrong scope. A handler from a
  scope that has already been retired is refused outright ("Not sent", nothing kept). Late answers for dropped entries are ignored and
  nothing is re-sent. (`authority_changed:<n>` is
  a same-account recheck and keeps entries.) Unmounting the component or disposing
  the kit cancels timers and ignores late answers, even before the first paint.
- `submit` throws only if the page is closed or 256 writes are unresolved. A request that is not JSON data
  (see below) is not thrown: it comes back "Not sent" with error code `invalid_request`, nothing kept.
  `writes.pending` is true while any write is being sent. Sent entries stay in
  `entries` until you `discard(id)` them; render only what you need.

Without Preact, `kit.createWriteHelper({ dispatch, busyDelaysMs?,
maxEntries?, scope? })` returns `{ submit, retry, discard, get, entries, subscribe,
dropAll, setScope, commit, restore, export, dispose }` with the same rules. `submit(request, { dispatch?, scope?, generation? })`
and `retry` return `{ id, done }`; `done` never rejects. Call `setScope(value)` (or
`dropAll()`) yourself when your account or workspace changes (the kit also calls
`dropAll` on `scope_changed` heard by a `useQueryFeed`) and `dispose()` when the
page closes. On a host still delivering
1.1.1, `kit.preact.useWrite` is undefined: feature-detect it and keep the old code.

### Keeping a write across a reload (1.4.0)

An app that saves its own state (for example through `setViewState`) can keep an unresolved
write and put it back after a reload, under its original key, so a Retry is applied once.
`export()` returns the unfinished writes to save and **permanently pins their keys**; `restore(saved)` puts one back.

```js
const writes = useWrite({ operation: 'create_record', scope: folder });
// Save whenever writes.entries changes (an effect on it is enough):
const toSave = writes.export();   // plain JSON: { request, key, madeAt, status, attempts, exposed, error? }
// After a reload, once your own account check has passed:
for (const saved of savedWrites) writes.restore(saved);   // { ok: true, entry } or { ok: false, code, message }
```

- **`restore` never sends.** Not now, not when the scope commits, not later by itself. Only the
  person's Retry (`retry(entry.id)`) sends a restored write, with the original key and the
  original frozen request.
- **`restore` takes only `uncertain` and `failed`.** `sent` and `pending` are refused (`invalid_status`).
  `export` does not lose an unfinished write: one **in flight** (dispatched, no answer yet) is exported as
  `uncertain` with `exposed: true`, because it may have applied; one **staged** under a render that has
  not committed (never dispatched) is exported as `failed`, `exposed: false`, error code `not_sent`, so it
  comes back as "Not sent" with Retry and Discard. `sent` writes are left out.
- **`exposed` says the key may have been applied.** `export` writes it (`true` for `uncertain`,
  `false` for `failed`). When it is missing or not a boolean, or the status is `uncertain`, the
  write is treated as exposed, **including for `failed`**: it comes back as `uncertain`
  ("May not have sent"), cannot be discarded, and keeps its key through every later refusal. Only an
  explicit `exposed: false` on a `failed` write restores it as `failed` ("Not sent", Retry and Discard).
- **An exported key is permanent.** Once an entry has appeared in an `export()` result, or was restored, it
  never takes another key, whatever answers come later, so a snapshot of it can never lead to a second
  application. This is structural, not a rule about when you save: `setViewState` is deferred and
  unacknowledged, so a reload can always bring back an older snapshot than the one you meant, and a
  refusal proves only that *that attempt* did not apply (Native checks access before it looks the key up,
  so a retry refused while access is revoked says nothing about before the snapshot). A retry of a
  restored or exported `failed` write therefore reuses its key (even if a key-making callback exports the entry
  while a new key is being made: the pinned key wins), which is harmless for a write Native never
  committed (Native replays only committed writes). Entries never exported keep the ordinary rule: a new key
  only after a definite, never-exposed failure.
- **Send as new is the person's explicit, informed choice.** If a permanently keyed `failed` write keeps being
  refused (say a node that replays a stored refusal for the key), the entry shows "Not sent" with Retry and
  Discard. Only after that write has been **refused in this page** (never straight from restored or exported
  state) does `canSendAsNew` become true. `sendAsNew(id, { acknowledgeMaySendTwice: true })` then discards it and
  submits the same request as a brand-new write under a fresh key; it does nothing without the acknowledgement.
  It can send the write **twice** if the first one in fact applied (a refusal says nothing about before your
  snapshot), so tell the person: `WriteStatus`'s `onSendAsNew` does a two-step confirm ("This may already have
  been sent. Sending it again could create a duplicate. Send again anyway?" with "Send again" and "Cancel"), and
  calls your handler only on "Send again", for the entry that was clicked: if another entry takes its place, or it stops being
  eligible, the question is cancelled. Pass the acknowledgement in that handler. It is offered only for
  `failed` writes, never `uncertain` ones, and never automatically; the old key stays retired.
- **A helper uses each key once.** It remembers the last 4,096 keys it has used, tracked or not, and
  `restore` refuses a saved entry under one of them (`superseded`). This covers a stale snapshot restored into
  the same page; after a real reload the new helper has used nothing.
- **The key is checked.** 1 to 128 letters, digits and `. _ : -`. The helper refuses a key (or id)
  it already holds, live, in flight, restored or sent (`duplicate_key`), so two writes never share
  a key. Ids are always new; they are never taken from saved state.
- **Scope.** A restored write belongs to the scope it is restored under, which is the committed
  scope unless you pass `scope` (the hook passes its render's). A scope that has already
  been replaced is refused (`scope_changed`). From a render that has not committed yet it waits:
  it is listed but `canRetry` is false until that render commits, and it is dropped if another
  scope commits. A change of account drops restored writes like any others. Save and check your
  own account identity next to the saved writes, and do not restore another account's.
- **`restore` never throws and changes nothing when it refuses.** Other codes: `invalid_key`,
  `superseded` (above), `invalid_request` (missing, or not JSON data), `invalid_entry` (made-at time, attempts or error unusable),
  `too_many`, `no_dispatch`, `closed`. It is safe to call from a subscriber or a dispatch.
- **`export` is plain, frozen and bounded, and anything it returns restores.** The helper holds at most
  256 writes (`maxEntries` above 256 is lowered to 256), so export returns at most 256 records; beyond that a
  new `submit` or `restore` is refused (`too_many`), and an unresolved write is never dropped. Only the current
  scope, error text cut to 32/64/500 characters, no internal fields; `attempts` is a whole number up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, where it stops. A key you
  pass to `submit` must follow the key rule above, or the write is "Not sent" before anything goes out.
  A request must survive `JSON.stringify` and `JSON.parse` as itself: objects, arrays (no holes), strings, finite
  numbers, booleans and null (a property that is `undefined` is left out, as JSON would). Each record's
  `request` is what was submitted, so your size limit applies.
- Agent sessions' own writes (`send`, `create`, `respond`) do not offer `restore` or `export`: a message or
  permission answer is not kept across a reload.
- Feature-detect: on a host still delivering 1.3.0 or older, `typeof writes.restore !== 'function'`.
  Keep your old persistence there.

### Agent sessions (1.3.0, Native Desktop only)

Paseo agent sessions are offered only by Native Desktop, and only to an app it has
admitted. Everywhere else `native.agentSessions` does not exist. `useAgentSessions`
checks for it, and reports `status: 'unsupported'` when it is absent, so an app carries
on without it (show nothing about sessions). The list, retry and epoch rules are the same
ones Attention and Focus use.

```js
const { useAgentSessions, FeedNotice, WriteStatus, html } = kit.preact;
function Sessions() {
  const s = useAgentSessions();
  if (s.status === 'unsupported') return null;
  return html`<${FeedNotice} feed=${s} />
    <ul>${s.sessions.map(x => html`<li key=${x.hostId + x.hostEpoch + x.id}>${x.title ?? 'Untitled'}</li>`)}</ul>
    <button onClick=${async () => {
      const host = s.hosts.find(h => h.status === 'reachable' && h.epoch);
      if (!host) return;
      const choice = await s.chooseFolder({ hostId: host.id, hostEpoch: host.epoch });
      if (choice.status === 'chosen') setFolder(choice.folder);
    }}>Choose a folder…</button>`;
}
```

- **The list.** `sessions` and `hosts` are the latest good list across the person's machines.
  `status` is `loading`, `ready`, `error` or `unsupported`. A transient failure (`unavailable`,
  `busy`) keeps the last good list on screen and reads it again quietly: after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 then
  every 30 seconds, at most 25 times and for at most 10 minutes, and not at all while the page is
  hidden. Nothing shows inside the first 4 seconds; then `notice` is `reconnecting`; once the
  retries are used up, or the answer is definite (`invalid`, `gone`), it is `failed`. Render
  `FeedNotice` with the hook's result: "Reconnecting…", or "Couldn't refresh" with Try again
  (`retry()`). The list stays live: a `listChanged` watch where the machine offers one and a
  slow poll otherwise.
- **Access refusals clear the list.** A `refused`, `invalid` or `gone` answer removes the
  sessions you were showing (a refusal must not keep showing what it refused). `refused` is still
  read again quietly, since Desktop can drop the app's launch handle and re-admit it, and the list
  comes back if it does.
- **Account boundary.** When any `useQueryFeed` hears `scope_changed`, the list is forgotten and
  read again from nothing, follows end, and every write is dropped. Anything still awaited across the
  change is dropped too: a follow that was starting delivers nothing, a folder choice answers `stale`, a
  catalog or `createStatus` answers `{ ok: false, code: 'unavailable' }`. `useAgentSessions` reads nothing
  until its component commits.
- **Machines and epochs.** A machine's `epoch` changing means its sessions were re-established, so a
  target that names the old epoch is dead. The hook drops those sessions, ends follows on that machine
  (the handler gets `{ kind: 'ended', code: 'gone' }`), and refuses to send to it:
  `isCurrent({ hostId, hostEpoch })` tells you, and a write to a dead epoch is "Not sent" without
  reaching the machine.
- **`chooseFolder({ hostId, hostEpoch })`** opens Desktop's chooser on that machine. Call it directly
  from the click. It resolves `{ status: 'chosen', hostId, hostEpoch, folder }`, `{ status: 'cancelled' }`,
  `{ status: 'stale', message }` (the machine reconnected while the person was choosing: choose again)
  or `{ status: 'unavailable', message }` (the machine does not offer it; update Native Desktop).
  One chooser is open at a time. A folder chosen this way can be the `workspaceId` of `create`.
- **Writes use the safe-write helper.** `send`, `create` and `respond` are each the same shape as
  `useWrite`: `entries`, `pending`, `submit`, `retry`, `discard`, and you render `WriteStatus`. There is
  no second retry model.
  - `send.submit({ hostId, hostEpoch, sessionId, text })` sends a message into a session.
  - `create.submit({ hostId, hostEpoch, provider, model, workspaceId, initialPrompt })` starts a session
    (get the choices from `catalog()`). `entry.result` is the new session once `sent`. The entry's `key`
    is the start's request id: after "May not have sent", `createStatus(entry.key)` asks Desktop what
    became of it (it needs a Desktop that offers that), and Retry sends the same request id again, which
    Desktop deduplicates.
  - `respond.submit({ hostId, hostEpoch, sessionId, permissionRequestId, action })` answers a pending
    permission (`session.pendingPermission.requestId`). Never invent a second key for it. Desktop refuses an
    operation key it has already seen, so an answer whose outcome is unknown is never sent again. The kit
    reads the session instead. The entry becomes "Sent" only on positive information: the machine is reachable at
    the same epoch, the session is in the list, and the session itself says the permission is no longer pending
    (`pendingPermission` is `null`, or another request). A missing session, an unreachable machine or an omitted
    `pendingPermission` prove nothing. Otherwise it stays "May not have sent" with no Retry (`canRetry` is false),
    and `entry.error.message` says to check in the session. It looks again every time the list changes, and
    nothing on screen changes while it is still undecided.
  - The helper's key is the host's `requestId` (or `operationKey`). An acknowledged answer is "Sent";
    a refusal, a request the machine could not take, or a request to a machine that has reconnected is
    "Not sent" and a Retry takes a new key; an answer Desktop calls `unknown` (or anything this kit does
    not recognise) is "May not have sent" and a Retry reuses the same key (except a permission answer, above). A started session whose answer
    is not a usable session is also "May not have sent".
  - A send that throws or is cut off after it was handed to Desktop is also "May not have sent" (same key), never "Not sent".
  - Call `submit` from the click: Desktop ties each of these to a user gesture, and the kit reaches it in
    the same task. For the same reason a busy machine is not retried on a timer; it is "Not sent" with Retry.
  - After a machine reconnects, discard a failed `create` and submit a new one from a fresh `catalog()`:
    the frozen request names the old epoch.
- `catalog()`, `follow(target, onEvent)`, `openConversation(target, { depth })` and `createStatus(requestId)`
  resolve `{ ok, value }` or `{ ok: false, code }`, never reject. `follow` returns `{ ok, value: { dispose } }`;
  dispose when leaving the view.

Without Preact, `kit.createAgentSessions({ noticeDelayMs? })` returns `{ state, subscribe, retry, isCurrent,
catalog, chooseFolder, follow, openConversation, createStatus, send, create, respond, dispose }`. `send`,
`create` and `respond` are write helpers (as `kit.createWriteHelper` returns); `state()` has the same fields
as the hook. Call `dispose()` when the page closes. On a host still delivering 1.2.0,
`kit.preact.useAgentSessions` and `kit.createAgentSessions` are undefined: feature-detect them and keep the
old code.

`Loading`, `Empty`, `ErrorState` (optional retry), `FeedNotice` (`feed`), `WriteStatus` (`entry`, `onRetry`, `onDiscard`), `PreviewBanner`, `Markdown`
(`source`), `Avatar` (initials), `IconSvg` (app-owned children), and `RecordLink`
(`id`) are supplied. Mount `PreviewBanner` only for known sample/preview mode.
Markdown reuses the kit parser: raw HTML stays text, images show alt text,
entities decode through an inert browser resolver, and navigation uses core
attributes and trusted user activation. No editor, comments or CSS are supplied.
Prepared documents retain their selected release. Kit bytes are exempt from
author size/digest accounting; source and declaration still define the app pin.


### Device snapshots and checkpoints (1.5.0)

Feature-detect `native.appState` after `kit.ready`; older hosts retain memory-only
writes and the app's view-state fallback. `kit.createAppState({schema})` tracks
revisions and serializes complete saves. Its value is `{entries, data?}`; each
entry has a permanent `key`. `load()` merges recovered sources by key and never
sends. `mergeData(current, incoming)` can merge drafts by their timestamps.
A null own snapshot never erases entries still in this page.

The adapter adopts whole sources in order while the successor fits 65,536 JSON
characters and consumes only those sources. Other entries remain in memory and
in their original device sources, retryable under their permanent keys. Save
again as entries settle to adopt the remainder. `save(value)` returns `status`,
`code`, the acknowledged `keys`, and the number of `deferred` sources. Never
silently remove unresolved entries to fit. Draft expiry belongs to the app.

Pass `checkpoint: entries => state.save({entries})` to `createWriteHelper` or
`useWrite`, after loading and restoring each saved entry with `restore`. The
helper freezes and pins each request/key, awaits this hook before dispatch,
and reports device custody only for keys returned by an acknowledged save.
A refusal still sends with memory custody and a visible `storageError`.
`WriteStatus` displays “Saved on this device” or explains that the page must
stay open. This is browser storage acknowledgement, not hosted sync.

Dispose the state adapter and helper when their account/workspace is retired.
Keep application metadata in entries if retry needs it (such as the operation,
audience, or parent). Restoring never dispatches; only an explicit Retry does.

Only one `createAppState` store may be open per app page: a second call throws
until the first store is disposed. Use `retire()` to clear this slot and dispose it while retaining unadopted sources; reopen after a scope retirement.
Changed deferred-source writes are copied into the own snapshot when room allows,
without consuming their sources. Duplicate keys keep the most exposed state,
then higher attempts, then later madeAt. When overflow prevents that copy, send
continues with memory custody and a not-saved notice. A crash can then reveal the
older unexposed source; discarding and retyping it can duplicate a send. Retry
under the permanent key instead. Checkpoints wait at most five seconds, including
queue time; the snapshot is exported when the queued checkpoint runs, after any
intervening settlement or discard. Change detection compares key, status,
exposure and attempts rather than JSON field order. Slack also publishes
view-state continuity while it fits. Over-limit saves trim the oldest drafts
first, then picked people and view preferences; only an outbox that still cannot fit uses
`continuity: null` to replace stale accepted work. Full live data remains in
memory and is passed to the device checkpoint. An independent warning names
what was omitted and clears when complete state fits; device-save success
alone cannot clear it. Finished Slack deliveries never regress during recovery. Rolling back to 1.4.0
hides device-only Slack work until re-upgrade; the device data remains saved.

The bridge currently closes all lanes on bfcache suspension. Restoring that bridge lifecycle is a separate follow-up.

Release `1.5.0`, major `1`, layer `core`. Factory `native.app-kit.core.factory.v1`; bridge `native.html.bridge.v1`.

JS SHA-256: `9407e4dc67e5e5dddb4d3c56e678d00b71de09c6bda3fa7274c94bff13e0aeec`

Types SHA-256: `03aba224585f08be6fbbe4d611deb5913ef8dc15a515725f43c42193b0645455`

```typescript
// Native core app kit — AGPL-3.0-only; Copyright Native contributors.
// Release 1.5.0; major 1; native.app-kit.core.factory.v1; native.html.bridge.v1
declare namespace NativeAppKit {
  interface KitRelease {
      readonly version: string;
      readonly major: number;
      readonly layer: "core";
      readonly factory: "native.app-kit.core.factory.v1";
      readonly bridge: "native.html.bridge.v1";
      readonly js_sha256: string;
      readonly types_sha256: string;
  }

  /** One result row, keyed by output column name. */
  type Row = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

  /**
   * One capped answer. `rows` is what was delivered; `truncated` says the
   * answer is a prefix. `rowCount` is a total only while `rowCountComplete` is
   * true, otherwise it is a floor ("more than N"). An app must show both.
   */
  interface QueryResult {
      readonly label: string;
      readonly columns: readonly string[];
      readonly rows: readonly Row[];
      readonly rowCount: number;
      readonly rowCountComplete: boolean;
      readonly truncated: boolean;
      /**
       * Set only on a result the host served from its cache, ahead of the
       * revalidation that follows it (a remount). It clears on the next uncached
       * delivery, even if the rows are equal. The host sends nothing for a
       * revalidation that finds equal rows, so then the flag stays set: do not
       * treat it as proof the rows are stale, only as "served from cache".
       */
      readonly cached?: boolean;
      /**
       * Set only on the `last` rows of an error feed whose subscription has ended
       * for good (a terminal error): nothing will refresh them, so they may be out
       * of date. They are kept for display; do not present them as current.
       */
      readonly stale?: boolean;
      /**
       * Only for the host-pushed keyed needs (`HOST_PUSHED_KEYED_NEEDS`): the
       * opaque handle the host minted for this parameter variant. The host names
       * it in `keyed_freshness.changed` when the variant's rows move.
       */
      readonly variant?: string;
  }

  /** Why a port call failed. Stable, app-facing; adapters map their transport onto it. */
  type PortErrorCode = "busy" | "timeout" | "undeclared" | "refused" | "unavailable" | "malformed" | "closed";

  /** Stable diagnostic shape; no transport or write capability. */
  interface KitError extends Error {
      readonly code: PortErrorCode;
      readonly detail?: string;
  }

  /** What a live subscription is showing right now. Errors keep the last good result. */
  type Feed<T> = {
      readonly status: "loading";
  } | {
      readonly status: "ready";
      readonly result: T;
  } | {
      readonly status: "error";
      readonly error: KitError;
      readonly last?: T;
  };

  /** Apps own DOM and CSS; all data comes from their declared snapshots. */
  interface CoreKitBase {
      readonly release: KitRelease;
      readonly ready: Promise<void>;
      read(key: string): Promise<QueryResult>;
      subscribe(key: string, listener: (feed: Feed<QueryResult>) => void): () => void;
      countLabel(result: QueryResult): string;
      errorText(error: Pick<KitError, "code">): string;
      recordLink(id: string): {
          readonly "data-native-record-id": string;
      };
      externalLink(url: string): {
          readonly "data-native-external-url": string;
      };
  }

  /** Structural UI types: source apps need no npm declarations. */
  type UiChild = object | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined | readonly UiChild[];

  type UiComponent<P = {}> = (props: P & {
      children?: UiChild;
  }) => UiChild;

  interface UiElement {
      readonly type: string | Function;
      readonly props: object;
      readonly key: string | number | null;
  }

  interface UiContext<T> {
      Provider: UiComponent<{
          value: T;
      }>;
      Consumer: UiComponent<{
          children: (value: T) => UiChild;
      }>;
  }

  type StateUpdate<T> = T | ((previous: T) => T);

  interface UiRef<T> {
      current: T;
  }

  type Effect = () => void | (() => void);

  interface AppQuery {
      readonly sql: string;
      readonly params?: readonly unknown[];
  }

  interface StepsQuery {
      readonly steps: readonly unknown[];
      readonly order?: string;
      readonly limit?: number;
      readonly offset?: number;
  }

  interface QueryFeedOptions {
      /** Waits before each quiet resubscribe after a transient terminal error; default 1, 2, 4, 8 s. */
      readonly retryDelaysMs?: readonly number[];
      /** How long a read may be in trouble before "Reconnecting…" shows; default 4 s. */
      readonly noticeDelayMs?: number;
      /** How long a recovery subscription may stay silent before "Couldn't refresh"; default 10 s. */
      readonly resubscribeDeadlineMs?: number;
  }

  interface AppQueryResult {
      readonly rows: readonly unknown[];
      readonly columns: readonly unknown[];
      readonly truncated: boolean;
      readonly cached?: boolean;
  }

  interface QueryFeedError {
      readonly code: string;
      readonly message: string;
      readonly terminal: boolean;
      /** Present while the kit is still recovering on its own: `quiet` inside the notice delay, `reconnecting` after it. Absent once recovery is over or cannot help. */
      readonly retrying?: 'quiet' | 'reconnecting';
  }

  type QueryFeedState = {
      readonly status: 'loading';
      readonly last?: AppQueryResult;
      readonly deliveredAt?: number;
  } | {
      readonly status: 'unsupported';
      readonly message: string;
  } | {
      readonly status: 'ready';
      readonly result: AppQueryResult;
      readonly deliveredAt: number;
  } | {
      readonly status: 'error';
      readonly error: QueryFeedError;
      readonly last?: AppQueryResult;
      readonly deliveredAt?: number;
  };

  /** What a person should be told about a failing read; never an internal outcome word. */
  type FeedNoticeKind = 'none' | 'reconnecting' | 'failed';

  type QueryFeed = QueryFeedState & {
      readonly retry: () => void;
      /** True when the rows shown (current or last good) are only part of the result. */
      readonly truncated: boolean;
      /** Quiet by design: `reconnecting` only after a delay, `failed` once retries are used up or cannot help. */
      readonly notice: FeedNoticeKind;
  };

  interface DispatchContext {
      /** Use as the idempotency key. */
      readonly key: string;
      /** 1 for the first dispatch of this write, then counting every retry. */
      readonly attempt: number;
  }

  interface WriteFailure {
      readonly status?: string;
      readonly code?: string;
      readonly message?: string;
  }

  /** An unfinished write as saved by `export` and given back to `restore`: plain and frozen. */
  interface ExportedWrite<Request = unknown> {
      /** The frozen request as submitted. */
      readonly request: Request;
      /** The idempotency key. Save it as it is. */
      readonly key: string;
      /** When the person made the change (ms since epoch). */
      readonly madeAt: number;
      readonly status: "uncertain" | "failed";
      readonly attempts: number;
      /** The key MAY have been applied: true for `uncertain`, false for `failed`. */
      readonly exposed: boolean;
      /** Status, code and message, each cut to a fixed length. */
      readonly error?: WriteFailure;
  }

  /** Options for `useWrite`. Give `operation` for an ordinary Native call, or `dispatch` to send it yourself. */
  interface UseWriteOptions<Request extends object = Record<string, unknown>, Result = unknown> {
      /** A Native operation such as `create_record`. The kit calls it with the frozen request plus the write's `idempotency_key`. */
      readonly operation?: string;
      /** Sends the request yourself and resolves when Native confirms. Use `context.key` as the idempotency key. Wins over `operation`. */
      readonly dispatch?: (request: Request, context: DispatchContext) => Promise<Result>;
      /** Extra tries after a `busy` refusal, spaced by these delays; default 300 ms then 600 ms. */
      readonly busyDelaysMs?: readonly number[];
      readonly checkpoint?: (entries: readonly ExportedWrite<Request>[]) => Promise<{
          readonly status: 'ok' | 'error';
          readonly keys?: readonly string[];
          readonly code?: string;
      }>;
      /** Any value that identifies the account or workspace the writes belong to. When it changes, every entry is dropped. */
      readonly scope?: unknown;
  }

  /** Where a write stands. A durable layer may add detail through `custody`, never new statuses. */
  type WriteStatus = "pending" | "sent" | "uncertain" | "failed";

  /** Who holds the request: `memory` is this page only. A durable layer may add values, so do not switch exhaustively. */
  type WriteCustody = "memory" | (string & {});

  /** A frozen snapshot of one logical write. A new snapshot replaces it on every change. */
  interface WriteEntry<Request = unknown, Result = unknown> {
      /** Stable for the life of the write, across retries and key changes. */
      readonly id: string;
      readonly status: WriteStatus;
      readonly custody: WriteCustody;
      /** Plain wording for `status`, honest about `custody`. Render this rather than your own copy. */
      readonly label: string;
      readonly custodyLabel?: string;
      readonly storageError?: string;
      /** The person's request exactly as frozen at submit; a retry sends this, never a re-read of the form. */
      readonly request: Request;
      /** The idempotency key the next (or current) dispatch uses. Changes only after a definite failure. */
      readonly key: string;
      readonly attempts: number;
      /** When the person made the change (ms since epoch). Provenance only; never used for ordering. */
      readonly madeAt: number;
      /** Why a write is `failed`, `uncertain` or applied with a pending receipt. */
      readonly error?: WriteFailure;
      /** What `dispatch` resolved with, once `sent`. */
      readonly result?: Result;
      readonly canRetry: boolean;
      readonly canDiscard: boolean;
      /** Refused again in this page under its permanent key: the person may send it as a new write (it may send twice). */
      readonly canSendAsNew: boolean;
  }

  /** Returned at once; `done` settles when this attempt ends. It never rejects. */
  interface WriteTicket<Request = unknown, Result = unknown> {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly done: Promise<WriteEntry<Request, Result>>;
  }

  /** Says the person has been told the write may already have been sent. */
  interface SendAsNewOptions {
      readonly acknowledgeMaySendTwice: true;
  }

  /** What `restore` takes: an `ExportedWrite`, or older state without `attempts` or `exposed`. */
  interface RestorableWrite<Request = unknown> {
      readonly request: Request;
      readonly key: string;
      readonly madeAt: number;
      /** Never `pending` or `sent`. */
      readonly status: "uncertain" | "failed";
      /** Default 1. */
      readonly attempts?: number;
      /** Default true, even for `failed`; true restores as `uncertain`. */
      readonly exposed?: boolean;
      readonly error?: WriteFailure;
  }

  type RestoreRefusalCode = "closed" | "invalid_status" | "invalid_key" | "invalid_request" | "invalid_entry" | "duplicate_key" | "superseded" | "scope_changed" | "too_many" | "no_dispatch";

  /** When `ok` is false nothing was kept and nothing was sent. */
  type RestoreResult<Request = unknown, Result = unknown> = {
      readonly ok: true;
      readonly entry: WriteEntry<Request, Result>;
  } | {
      readonly ok: false;
      readonly code: RestoreRefusalCode;
      readonly message: string;
  };

  interface UseWrite<Request extends object = Record<string, unknown>, Result = unknown> {
      /** Every write still on screen, oldest first. Render each with `WriteStatus`. */
      readonly entries: readonly WriteEntry<Request, Result>[];
      /** True while any write is being sent. */
      readonly pending: boolean;
      /** Freezes the request, mints its key and sends it in this task (call it from the click). Throws only if closed or 256 writes are unresolved. */
      submit(request: Request): WriteTicket<Request, Result>;
      /** Sends the same frozen request again, under the same key (a new key only for a failed write that was never exported). */
      retry(id: string): WriteTicket<Request, Result> | undefined;
      /** Removes a `failed` or `sent` entry; an uncertain one stays until it resolves. */
      discard(id: string): boolean;
      /** As `WriteHelper.sendAsNew`: may send twice; requires acknowledgement. */
      sendAsNew(id: string, acknowledgement: SendAsNewOptions): WriteTicket<Request, Result> | undefined;
      /** As `WriteHelper.restore` (1.4.0). */
      restore(saved: RestorableWrite<Request>): RestoreResult<Request, Result>;
      /** As `WriteHelper.export`: permanently pins the keys it returns. */
      export(): readonly ExportedWrite<Request>[];
  }

  interface AgentSessionsOptions {
      /** How long a list may be in trouble before "Reconnecting…" shows; default 4 s. */
      readonly noticeDelayMs?: number;
  }

  /** What an agent asks of the person. `done` is the agent saying it has finished something to look at. */
  type AttentionRequestKind = "blocked" | "decision" | "review" | "done";

  interface SessionAttentionRequest {
      readonly kind: AttentionRequestKind;
      readonly message: string;
  }

  type PendingPermissionKind = "question" | "plan" | "tool" | "mode" | "other";

  /** An advisory only: `requestId` is an opaque identifier and there is no description, only a kind and an optional title. */
  interface SessionPendingPermission {
      readonly requestId: string;
      readonly kind: PendingPermissionKind;
      readonly title?: string;

  interface SessionSummary {

      readonly hostId: string;

  interface SessionHostCapabilities {

  interface SessionHost {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly label: string;
      readonly status: "reachable" | "unreachable";

      readonly capabilities?: SessionHostCapabilities;

  type SessionRefusal = "refused" | "invalid" | "unavailable" | "gone" | "busy";

  interface AgentSessionsError {

      /** Present while the kit is still reading the list again by itself: `quiet` inside the notice delay, `reconnecting` after it. */
      readonly retrying?: 'quiet' | 'reconnecting';
  }

  /** What a person should be told about the session list; the same shape of answer `useQueryFeed` gives for a read. */

      readonly hosts: readonly SessionHost[];

  /** The host does not offer `agentSessions` (only Native Desktop does, to an app it has admitted). Nothing else will happen. */
   | {

      readonly message: string;
      readonly sessions: readonly SessionSummary[];
      readonly hosts: readonly SessionHost[];
      readonly notice: FeedNoticeKind;
      readonly listedAt: number | null;

      readonly status: 'ready';
      readonly sessions: readonly SessionSummary[];
      readonly hosts: readonly SessionHost[];
      readonly notice: FeedNoticeKind;
      readonly listedAt: number | null;

  /** `sessions` are the last good list, kept through a transient failure and cleared by an access refusal. */
   | {
      readonly status: 'error';
      readonly error: AgentSessionsError;
      readonly sessions: readonly SessionSummary[];
      readonly hosts: readonly SessionHost[];
      readonly notice: FeedNoticeKind;
      readonly listedAt: number | null;
  };

  /** A session is addressed by host, host epoch and id together. */
  interface SessionTarget {
      readonly hostId: string;
      readonly hostEpoch: string;
      readonly sessionId: string;
  }

  type SessionResult<T> = {
      readonly ok: true;
      readonly value: T;
  } | {
      readonly ok: false;
      readonly code: SessionRefusal;
  };

  interface SessionCatalogModel {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly label: string;
      readonly description?: string;
      readonly featured?: boolean;
      readonly isDefault?: boolean;
      readonly thinkingOptions: readonly {
          readonly id: string;
          readonly label: string;
      }[];
      readonly defaultThinkingOptionId?: string;
  }

  interface SessionCatalogProvider {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly label: string;
      readonly available: boolean;
      readonly unavailableReason?: string;
      readonly models: readonly SessionCatalogModel[];
      readonly modes: readonly {
          readonly id: string;
          readonly label: string;
          readonly description?: string;
      }[];
      readonly defaultModeId?: string;
  }

  interface SessionCatalogWorkspace {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly name: string;
      readonly path: string;
      readonly projectName?: string;
      readonly isGitRepo?: boolean;
      readonly kind?: "ordinary" | "folder" | "worktree";
  }

  interface SessionCatalogHost {
      readonly hostId: string;
      readonly hostLabel: string;
      readonly hostEpoch: string | null;

  interface SessionCatalog {
      readonly hosts: readonly SessionCatalogHost[];

  /** What choosing a folder came to. */
  type FolderChoice = {
      readonly status: "chosen";
      readonly hostId: string;
      readonly hostEpoch: string;
      readonly folder: SessionCatalogWorkspace;
  } | {
      readonly status: "cancelled";
  }
  /** The machine reconnected while the person was choosing: the choice belongs to a world that no longer exists. Choose again. */
   | {
      readonly status: "stale";
      readonly message: string;
  } | {
      readonly status: "unavailable";
      readonly message: string;
  };

  /** Projected timeline only: messages contain at most 16 Ki UTF-16 code units, no raw tool payloads. */
  type SessionTimelineItem = {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly kind: "message";
      readonly role: "user" | "assistant";
      readonly text: string;
  } | {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly kind: "tool";
      readonly title: string;
      readonly status: string;
      readonly detail?: string;
  } | {
      readonly id: string;
      readonly kind: "status";
      readonly status: string;
  };

  /** Snapshot replaces the view; updates contain changed items; resync asks the app to re-follow. */
  type SessionEvent = SessionTarget & ({
      readonly kind: "snapshot" | "update";
      readonly items: readonly SessionTimelineItem[];
  } | {
      readonly kind: "resync";
  } | {
      readonly kind: "ended";
      readonly code: SessionRefusal;
  });

  interface SessionSubscription {
      readonly dispose: () => void;
  }

  type SessionCreateState = "unknown_request" | "preparing" | "confirming" | "dispatching" | "dispatched" | "settled" | "cancelled" | "terminal_mismatch" | "refused_retryable";

  type SessionCreateErrorCode = "invalid_request" | "refused" | "busy" | "host_unreachable" | "host_epoch_changed" | "create_unsupported" | "provider_unavailable" | "model_unavailable" | "workspace_not_found" | "worktree_unsupported" | "create_failed" | "outcome_unknown";

  type SessionCreateResult = {
      readonly ok: true;
      readonly value: SessionSummary;
  } | {
      readonly ok: false;
      readonly error: {
          readonly code: SessionCreateErrorCode;
          readonly message: string;
      };
  };

  interface SessionCreateStatus {
      readonly state: SessionCreateState;
      readonly result?: SessionCreateResult;
  }

  /** Everything but the list. Targets come from the list's own sessions and hosts. */
  interface AgentSessionsActions {
      /** Whether this machine is still the one the list showed, at the same epoch. A target that is not current is dead: do not send to it. */
      isCurrent(target: Pick<SessionTarget, 'hostId' | 'hostEpoch'>): boolean;
      /** The machines, agents, models and folders a session can be started with. */
      catalog(): Promise<SessionResult<SessionCatalog>>;
      /**
       * Open Desktop's folder chooser on a machine. Call it directly from the click. Resolves with the folder, `cancelled`, `stale`
       * (the machine reconnected while the person was choosing, so the choice is dropped) or `unavailable`.
       */
      chooseFolder(host: Pick<SessionTarget, 'hostId' | 'hostEpoch'>): Promise<FolderChoice>;
      /** Follow a session's timeline. Ends with an `ended` event if its machine reconnects. Dispose when leaving the view. */
      follow(target: SessionTarget, onEvent: (event: SessionEvent) => void): Promise<SessionResult<SessionSubscription>>;
      /** Open the conversation in Desktop: `quick` in the side pane (default), `full` in the Agent HQ window. */
      openConversation(target: SessionTarget, options?: {
          readonly depth?: 'quick' | 'full';
      }): Promise<SessionResult<Record<string, never>>>;
      /** What became of a start whose outcome is unknown; pass the write entry's `key`. Needs a Desktop that offers it. */
      createStatus(requestId: string): Promise<SessionResult<SessionCreateStatus>>;
  }

  /**
   * Words that came from someone else, sent beside the person's own `text` so the Desktop can frame them as data rather
   * than as the person's instruction (design 86a586b section 8). At most 8 items; `from` 1..32 characters, `text` 1..12288
   * non-blank. `sourceMessageId`, when present, is an owner-claimed reference to the quoted message
   * (design f38936b §7.3, Desktop S5i contract.ts): canonical lowercase UUID, never authenticated authorship
   * nor a read grant. Only a host that offers `app.agent-sessions.adopted.v1` takes them; elsewhere a send that carries any
   * resolves `unavailable` and sends nothing, so put quoted words in `text` only if you accept that they read as the person's.
   */
  interface SessionQuoted {
      readonly from: string;
      readonly text: string;
      readonly sourceMessageId?: string;
  }

  interface SessionSendRequest extends SessionTarget {
      readonly text: string;
      readonly contentOrigin?: "typed" | "generated";
      readonly quoted?: readonly SessionQuoted[];
  }

  /** `acknowledged`: Desktop took it. `unknown`: it may have arrived; never assume either way. */
  interface SessionReceipt {
      readonly requestId: string;
      readonly delivery: "acknowledged" | "unknown";
  }

  interface SessionCreateInput {
      readonly requestId: string;
      readonly hostId: string;
      readonly hostEpoch: string;
      readonly provider: string;
      readonly model: string;
      readonly workspaceId: string;
      readonly modeId?: string;
      readonly thinkingOptionId?: string;
      readonly newWorktree?: {
          readonly baseBranch: string;
      };
      /** Non-blank, at most 16 KiB UTF-8. */
      readonly initialPrompt: string;
      readonly contentOrigin?: "typed" | "generated";
      readonly quoted?: readonly SessionQuoted[];
  }

  type SessionCreateRequest = Omit<SessionCreateInput, "requestId">;

  type SessionPermissionAction = {
      readonly kind: "tool_decision";
      readonly behavior: "allow" | "deny";
  } | {
      readonly kind: "plan_action";
      readonly actionId: string;
  } | {
      readonly kind: "question_dismiss";
  } | {
      readonly kind: "question_answers";
      readonly answers: readonly {
          readonly questionIndex: number;
          readonly optionIndexes?: readonly number[];
          readonly text?: string;
      }[];
  };

  interface SessionPermissionRequest extends SessionTarget {
      /** The pending permission's `requestId`, from the session summary. */
      readonly permissionRequestId: string;
      readonly action: SessionPermissionAction;
  }

  /** What the host said about a permission response. Only `acknowledged` resolves a write. */
  interface SessionPermissionAnswer {
      readonly status: "acknowledged";
  }

  /**
   * The Paseo agent sessions `useAgentSessions` reads and acts on (1.3.0). `status` is `unsupported` when the host does not offer
   * `agentSessions`; the rest follows `useQueryFeed`: `sessions` is the last good list, kept through a transient failure and
   * cleared by an access refusal, and `notice` says when to speak.
   */
  type UseAgentSessions = AgentSessionsState & AgentSessionsActions & {
      /** Read the list now. */
      readonly retry: () => void;
      /** Send a message into a session (`submit` from the click). Render each entry with `WriteStatus`. */
      readonly send: Omit<UseWrite<SessionSendRequest, SessionReceipt>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
      /** Start a session (`submit` from the click). The entry's `key` is the start's request id, for `createStatus`. */
      readonly create: Omit<UseWrite<SessionCreateRequest, SessionSummary>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
      /** Answer a session's pending permission (`submit` from the click). */
      readonly respond: Omit<UseWrite<SessionPermissionRequest, SessionPermissionAnswer>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
  };

  interface PreactKit {
      h<P>(type: string | UiComponent<P>, props: P | null, ...children: UiChild[]): UiElement;
      render(child: UiChild, parent: Element | Document | ShadowRoot): void;
      readonly Fragment: UiComponent;
      createContext<T>(value: T): UiContext<T>;
      html(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): UiChild;
      useState<T>(initial: T | (() => T)): [
          T,
          (value: StateUpdate<T>) => void
      ];
      useState<T = undefined>(): [
          T | undefined,
          (value: StateUpdate<T | undefined>) => void
      ];
      useReducer<S, A>(reducer: (state: S, action: A) => S, initial: S): [
          S,
          (action: A) => void
      ];
      useReducer<S, A, I>(reducer: (state: S, action: A) => S, initial: I, init: (initial: I) => S): [
          S,
          (action: A) => void
      ];
      useRef<T>(initial: T): UiRef<T>;
      useRef<T>(initial: T | null): UiRef<T | null>;
      useRef<T = undefined>(): UiRef<T | undefined>;
      useEffect(effect: Effect, dependencies?: readonly unknown[]): void;
      useLayoutEffect(effect: Effect, dependencies?: readonly unknown[]): void;
      useMemo<T>(factory: () => T, dependencies: readonly unknown[]): T;
      useCallback<T extends Function>(callback: T, dependencies: readonly unknown[]): T;
      useContext<T>(context: UiContext<T>): T;
      useImperativeHandle<T>(ref: UiRef<T> | ((value: T | null) => void) | null, create: () => T, dependencies?: readonly unknown[]): void;
      useDebugValue<T>(value: T, format?: (value: T) => unknown): void;
      useErrorBoundary(callback?: (error: unknown, info: unknown) => void): [
          unknown,
          () => void
      ];
      useId(): string;
      useFeed(key: string): Feed<QueryResult>;
      /** Query must be JSON serializable; equivalent values share a subscription. */
      useQueryFeed(query: AppQuery | StepsQuery, options?: QueryFeedOptions): QueryFeed;
      /** Renders `feed.notice` ("Reconnecting…", or "Couldn't refresh" with Try again) and a partial-results line. */
      readonly FeedNotice: UiComponent<{
          feed: Pick<QueryFeed, 'notice' | 'retry'> & {
              readonly truncated?: boolean;
              readonly error?: {
                  readonly code: string;
                  readonly terminal?: boolean;
              };
          };
      }>;
      /**
       * Safe writes (1.2.0). Freezes each request, mints its idempotency key before anything is sent, retries `busy`
       * a bounded number of times, and tracks `pending | sent | uncertain | failed`. Memory only: nothing survives a reload.
       * Entries are dropped when the app's account or workspace changes (`scope_changed` on any `useQueryFeed`, or `scope`).
       */
      useWrite<Request extends object = Record<string, unknown>, Result = unknown>(options: UseWriteOptions<Request, Result>): UseWrite<Request, Result>;
      /** "Sending…", "Sent", "May not have sent" with Retry, or "Not sent" with Retry and Discard. */
      readonly WriteStatus: UiComponent<{
          entry: Pick<WriteEntry, 'status' | 'label' | 'canRetry' | 'canDiscard'> & {
              canSendAsNew?: boolean;
              id?: string;
              key?: string;
              custodyLabel?: string;
              storageError?: string;
          };
          onRetry?: () => void;
          onDiscard?: () => void;
          onSendAsNew?: () => void;
          className?: string;
      }>;
      /**
       * Paseo agent sessions (1.3.0, Native Desktop only): the live list, the folder chooser, and start/send/answer-a-permission as safe writes.
       * Reports `unsupported` when the host does not offer `agentSessions`. Needs `useQueryFeed`'s account boundary too: a `scope_changed` on any
       * feed forgets the list and drops every write. Render `FeedNotice` with it.
       */
      useAgentSessions(options?: AgentSessionsOptions): UseAgentSessions;
      readonly Loading: UiComponent<{
          what?: string;
      }>;
      readonly Empty: UiComponent;
      /** Renders nothing while `error.retrying` is `quiet`, "Reconnecting…" while it is `reconnecting`, otherwise the full error with Try again. */
      readonly ErrorState: UiComponent<{
          error: Pick<KitError, 'code'> & {
              message?: string;
              retrying?: 'quiet' | 'reconnecting';
          };
          onRetry?: () => void;
      }>;
      /** Mount only when the host explicitly identifies sample/preview mode. */
      readonly PreviewBanner: UiComponent;
      readonly Markdown: UiComponent<{
          source: string;
          className?: string;
      }>;
      readonly Avatar: UiComponent<{
          name?: string;
          initials?: string;
          title?: string;
          className?: string;
      }>;
      readonly IconSvg: UiComponent<{
          children?: UiChild;
          title?: string;
          viewBox?: string;
          className?: string;
      }>;
      readonly RecordLink: UiComponent<{
          id: string;
          children?: UiChild;
          className?: string;
      }>;
  }

  /** A bounded, acknowledged device snapshot. Entries merge by permanent key. */
  interface AppStateEntry {
      readonly key: string;
      readonly exposed?: boolean;
      readonly status?: string;
      readonly state?: string;
      readonly attempts?: number;
      readonly madeAt?: number;
      readonly at?: string;
  }

  interface AppStateValue<Entry extends AppStateEntry = AppStateEntry, Data = unknown> {
      readonly entries: readonly Entry[];
      readonly data?: Data;
  }

  interface AppStateOptions<Entry extends AppStateEntry, Data> {
      readonly schema: string;
      readonly initial?: AppStateValue<Entry, Data>;
      /** Merge application data (for example drafts) from recovered sources. */
      readonly mergeData?: (current: Data | undefined, incoming: Data | undefined) => Data | undefined;
  }

  interface AppStateSaveResult {
      readonly status: 'ok' | 'error';
      readonly code?: string;
      /** Only these keys were in the acknowledged successor. */
      readonly keys: readonly string[];
      readonly deferred: number;
  }

  interface AppState<Entry extends AppStateEntry = AppStateEntry, Data = unknown> {
      /** Merge own and recovered values, never sending. Null never erases this page's memory. */
      load(): Promise<AppStateValue<Entry, Data>>;
      /** Save a complete live value; retain overflow sources until room frees. */
      save(value: AppStateValue<Entry, Data>): Promise<AppStateSaveResult>;
      value(): AppStateValue<Entry, Data>;
      result(): AppStateSaveResult;
      /** Retire this slot only, keeping unadopted source snapshots; then dispose. */
      retire(): Promise<AppStateSaveResult>;
      dispose(): void;
  }

  interface WriteHelperOptions<Request, Result> {
      /** Await a device checkpoint before dispatch. Refusal still sends, with memory custody. */
      checkpoint?(entries: readonly ExportedWrite<Request>[]): Promise<{
          readonly status: 'ok' | 'error';
          readonly keys?: readonly string[];
          readonly code?: string;
      }>;
      /** Send the request; resolve when Native confirms, reject with the host's error. `SubmitOptions.dispatch` wins. */
      dispatch?(request: Request, context: DispatchContext): Promise<Result>;
      /** Delays before each extra try after a `busy` refusal. Default 300, 600 ms; `[]` for none. */
      busyDelaysMs?: readonly number[];
      /** Unresolved writes to keep; the oldest `sent` entries are forgotten first. Default and largest 256. */
      maxEntries?: number;
      /** Subscribe to account/workspace changes; call the callback to drop everything. Returns the unsubscribe. */
      onScopeChange?(drop: () => void): () => void;
      /** The account/workspace the writes belong to now (compared with `Object.is`). */
      scope?: unknown;
      /** Injectable for tests. */
      now?(): number;
  }

  interface SubmitOptions {
      /** Use this idempotency key for the first dispatch (it was minted by the caller before the request was built). */
      readonly key?: string;
      /** Sends this write, and every retry of it, even if the helper's own `dispatch` or the app's options change later. */
      readonly dispatch?: (request: never, context: DispatchContext) => Promise<unknown>;
      /** The scope this write is made in; default the current one. A UI passes its render's scope. */
      readonly scope?: unknown;
      /** The render generation of the handler (see `commit`). A newer one than committed is staged until it commits. Omit outside UI hooks. */
      readonly generation?: number;
  }

  interface RestoreOptions {
      /** Sends the write on retry; default the helper's `dispatch`. */
      readonly dispatch?: (request: never, context: DispatchContext) => Promise<unknown>;
      /** The scope the state belongs to; default the current one. */
      readonly scope?: unknown;
      /** As `SubmitOptions.generation`; until it commits the entry cannot be retried. */
      readonly generation?: number;
  }

  interface WriteHelper<Request = unknown, Result = unknown> {
      /** Freeze, key and dispatch in the caller's task, so a host that ties a write to a click still sees one. */
      submit(request: Request, options?: SubmitOptions): WriteTicket<Request, Result>;
      /** Send the same frozen request again. No-op while pending or after `sent`. Undefined for an unknown id. */
      retry(id: string): WriteTicket<Request, Result> | undefined;
      /** Forget a `failed` or `sent` entry. An `uncertain` one cannot be: its key protects against a duplicate. */
      discard(id: string): boolean;
      get(id: string): WriteEntry<Request, Result> | undefined;
      entries(): readonly WriteEntry<Request, Result>[];
      subscribe(listener: (entries: readonly WriteEntry<Request, Result>[]) => void): () => void;
      /** An account or workspace change: forget everything, send nothing more for it, ignore late answers. */
      dropAll(code?: string): void;
      /** Tell the helper which account/workspace is current. A different value drops every entry; nothing is sent under another scope. */
      setScope(scope: unknown): void;
      /** Publish a render generation and scope, from a layout effect (never while rendering). Staged writes go out if their scope is committed, else are dropped. */
      commit(generation: number, scope: unknown): void;
      /** Put a saved write back (1.4.0). It never sends: only `retry` does, under the saved key. Refuses with a code; never throws. */
      restore(saved: RestorableWrite<Request>, options?: RestoreOptions): RestoreResult<Request, Result>;
      /** The unfinished entries of this scope to save (in flight is `uncertain`, staged is `failed`). Permanently pins the keys it returns. */
      export(): readonly ExportedWrite<Request>[];
      /** May send twice; requires acknowledgement. Replaces a `canSendAsNew` write with the same request under a new key. */
      sendAsNew(id: string, acknowledgement: SendAsNewOptions): WriteTicket<Request, Result> | undefined;
      /** Cancel timers, ignore late answers, send nothing more. Idempotent. */
      dispose(): void;
  }

  /** The framework-free sessions surface. Writes use the same lifecycle as `createWriteHelper`: render `entry.label`, switch on `entry.status`. */
  interface AgentSessionsClient extends AgentSessionsActions {
      state(): AgentSessionsState;
      subscribe(listener: (state: AgentSessionsState) => void): () => void;
      /** Read the list now ("Try again"). */
      retry(): void;
      /** Send a message into a session. Call `submit` from the click. */
      readonly send: Omit<WriteHelper<SessionSendRequest, SessionReceipt>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
      /** Start a session. Call `submit` from the click. */
      readonly create: Omit<WriteHelper<SessionCreateRequest, SessionSummary>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
      /** Answer a session's pending permission. Call `submit` from the click. */
      readonly respond: Omit<WriteHelper<SessionPermissionRequest, SessionPermissionAnswer>, 'restore' | 'export'>;
      /** Stop reading and drop every write. Call when the page closes. */
      dispose(): void;
  }

  interface CoreKit extends CoreKitBase {
      readonly preact: PreactKit;
      /** Device snapshots with revision tracking and selective whole-source recovery (1.5.0). */
      createAppState<Entry extends AppStateEntry, Data = unknown>(options: AppStateOptions<Entry, Data>): AppState<Entry, Data>;
      /**
       * Safe writes without a UI framework (1.2.0): see `preact.useWrite` for what it does. You send the request
       * (`dispatch`), and call `dropAll()` yourself when your account or workspace changes; the kit does that for
       * you when a `useQueryFeed` hears `scope_changed`. Call `dispose()` when the page closes.
       */
      createWriteHelper<Request extends object = Record<string, unknown>, Result = unknown>(options: Omit<WriteHelperOptions<Request, Result>, 'onScopeChange' | 'now'>): WriteHelper<Request, Result>;
      /**
       * Paseo agent sessions without a UI framework (1.3.0; see `preact.useAgentSessions`): the live list, `chooseFolder`, and start/send/answer
       * as safe writes. Its `state().status` is `unsupported` when the host does not offer `agentSessions`. The kit forgets the list and drops
       * every write when a `useQueryFeed` hears `scope_changed`. Call `dispose()` when the page closes.
       */
      createAgentSessions(options?: AgentSessionsOptions): AgentSessionsClient;
  }

  interface AppStateEnvelope<Entry extends AppStateEntry, Data> {
      readonly value: AppStateValue<Entry, Data>;
      readonly source?: string;
  }

  interface AppStateHost {
      get(options: {
          schema: string;
      }): Promise<{
          status: 'ok';
          revision: number;
          snapshot: AppStateEnvelope<AppStateEntry, unknown> | null;
          recovered: readonly AppStateEnvelope<AppStateEntry, unknown>[];
      } | {
          status: 'error';
          code: string;
      }>;
      clear?(options: {
          expectedRevision: number;
          consume: readonly string[];
      }): Promise<{
          status: 'ok';
          revision: number;
      } | {
          status: 'error';
          code: string;
      }>;
      set(value: unknown, options: {
          schema: string;
          expectedRevision: number;
          consume: readonly string[];
      }): Promise<{
          status: 'ok';
          revision: number;
      } | {
          status: 'error';
          code: string;
      }>;
  }

  type QueryDelivery = (AppQueryResult & {
      readonly status: 'ready';
  }) | {
      readonly status: 'error';
      readonly code: string;
      readonly message: string;
      readonly terminal: boolean;
  };

  interface AppCall {
      readonly request_id: string;
      readonly confirmed: Promise<unknown>;
  }

  /** Data methods exist only after app-v2 negotiation; kit policy grants no data authority. */
  interface Host {
      readonly appState?: AppStateHost;
      readonly kit?: CoreKit;
      query?(query: AppQuery | StepsQuery): Promise<AppQueryResult>;
      subscribe?(query: AppQuery | StepsQuery, listener: (delivery: QueryDelivery) => void): () => void;
      call?(operation: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>): AppCall;
  }
}
interface Window { readonly native?: NativeAppKit.Host }
```
